RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

An all-female panel alone is not evidence of discrimination; panels typically reflect available departmental leaders and HR staff. Once candidates reach the final interview stage, decisions rarely hinge purely on degrees or years of experience. For director-level positions, panels heavily prioritize interview performance, leadership style, public consultation experience, and organizational fit. 

Raising gender bias without concrete evidence—such as inappropriate questions or clear procedural breaches—will appear unfounded and could damage your professional reputation in municipal government. Delays in written debriefs are common in public sector hiring. Instead of alleging bias, send a polite follow-up requesting constructive feedback on how to strengthen your candidacy for future executive roles.
